correctness.rationale: For p(i)=1 iff i=2^j-1, the least failed-prefix greedy attractor initially marks 0,2. After mark h=3a-1 with a=2^k, every trailing word p[3a..j] for 3a<=j<6a-1 has a prior occurrence shifted by 2a, so no new mark is needed. At j=6a-1 the first zero factor of length 2a lies wholly beyond earlier marks, forcing a new mark. Induction establishes marks {0}∪{3*2^k-1}; direct dyadic counting yields g(N)=1 for N=1,2, else 2+floor(log2(N/3)). Independent word/factor tests checked 80 prefixes and exact z-factor phrase-end equality for eight phrases; proof is unrestricted and independent of these finite tests.
